newsitem.title: UK: Prompt dirty tankers steady, forward rates seen ea.
newsitem.headline: Prompt dirty tankers steady, forward rates seen ea.

text.p: Dirty tanker chartering was slower on Thursday after fairly active trade this week.
Brokers said rates were mostly unchanged although those for Suezmax tonnage on some transatlantic routes were traded at slightly lower levels after a lull in demand.

A West African Suezmax cargo was booked for mid-Nov voyage to the U.S. Gulf at W102.5, around 2-1/2 points down on recent assessments although at parity with last traded levels. The vessel was also booked with options to UKC-Med at W107.5 and USAC at W105.
Traders expect rates to continue soft with a growing surplus of available tonnage seen around early to mid-November after recently slow transatlantic trade from West Africa and the North Sea.
However, the Mideast Gulf and Red Sea region continues to be a draw for the larger VLCC/ULCC type vessels with both finding work to the East.

Rates here for 260,000 tonne vessels have been fairly stable all week with active trade seen to Singapore and the Philippines at around W47.5 while rates for voyages to South Korea firmed around three points to trade at W53 for an early November cargo.
A growing surplus of unchartered tonnage was expected as slowing demand and easing rates in NWE see vessels returning to the Mediterranean, but prompt markets remained buoyant.
"A combination of slowing demand and quick turnaround voyages may leave vessels looking for work," a broker said.
But he saw sufficient Black Sea and cross-Med trade to provide short-term support.
In the western hemisphere Caribbean upcoast U.S. business remained fairly active but rates to the U.S. Gulf were hard to pin down with several cargoes booked but few rates reported.
